gap: No result ChatGPT got states hours per charge for each TMR board under $100 worked out from capacity and a named reviewer's runtime: about 3 h for the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR at 8K 2.4 GHz with LEDs (Notebookcheck), about 30 h for the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR at 1,000 Hz with RGB (APH Networks), and 32 to 56 h for the Gamakay TK75 TMR with RGB and display on (Smartzone).
standout_why: Compared against Notebookcheck (has the FUN60's 3 h and 4,000 mAh but no other board), PCWorld (only "a few hours" and 4,000 mAh), keyboardtester.click (lists mAh for five TMR boards, no runtime for any board under $100, TK75 TMR at $109.99), MKB Guide (no battery or price figures), the RTINGS 60% list (only a link to the FUN60 Ultra in the text returned) and HLPlanet's TMR vs Hall page (no battery figures, TK75 TMR at $114.99). None puts the under-$100 boards side by side on runtime, none carries Smartzone's TK75 TMR runtime, and none shows the TK75 TMR at $89.99. Not a 3 because the three runtimes were taken under different conditions and Smartzone does not name its connection mode.
decides: It splits the pick by use. ChatGPT's own caveat on the FUN60 Ultra TMR is short battery life at 8K wireless; the derived figure puts that at under half of one 8-hour day per charge, against 4 to 7 such days for the Gamakay TK75 TMR with lighting on. For a shopper who wants a wireless TMR board under $100, that moves the TK75 TMR ($89.99 at Gamakay today, under $100 only at the sale price) ahead of the FUN60 Ultra tri-mode. The FUN60 keeps the wired and 60% case, and the HE65 V2 TMR keeps the lowest-price case if its $59.99 is confirmed. The Womier K75 TMR drops out at its maker's store ($119.99).

findings.label: Runtime per charge at 2.4 GHz 8K, LEDs lit
findings.value: about 3 h (Notebookcheck); 3 h / 8 h = 0.4 of an 8-hour day
findings.source_title: MonsGeek Fun60 Ultra TMR hands-on review: Rapid trigger keyboard with 8 kHz wireless polling made affordable - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck: "With the LEDs lit, it can be around 3 hours"; it also reports around 4 to 5 hours on Bluetooth. Battery 4,000 mAh, weight 1,023 g, 60 keys in its spec table. Implied average draw: 4,000 mAh / 3 h = about 1,333 mAh per hour.

findings.label: Second named reviewer on 8K wireless runtime
findings.value: "often only lasted a few hours in this high-performance mode" (PCWorld), 4,000 mAh
findings.source_title: Monsgeek FUN60 Ultra review: The TMR-powered keyboard everyone needs | PCWorld
findings.note: No hour figure; PCWorld says the battery lasts "for days" on Bluetooth or with dimmed lighting. Agrees in direction with Notebookcheck's 3 h.

findings.label: Runtime per charge, RGB and display on
findings.value: 32 to 56 h (4 to 7 days x 8 h per day, Smartzone, Max Drechsel)
findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75 TMR Test: Ultraleise 75%-Tastatur für Büro & Gaming - Smartzone
findings.note: Review dated 2026-08-15. "hält die Tastatur bei acht Stunden Nutzung etwa vier bis sieben Tage durch" with display and RGB on. Smartzone does not state the connection mode or polling rate for this figure, so it is not like-for-like with Notebookcheck's 8K 2.4 GHz test. Implied draw: 8,000 mAh / 32 to 56 h = 143 to 250 mAh per hour. Against the FUN60's 3 h: 32/3 = 10.7x to 56/3 = 18.7x.

findings.label: Runtime per charge, RGB and display off, scan rates at maximum
findings.value: up to 160 h (20 days x 8 h per day, Smartzone)
findings.source_title: Gamakay TK75 TMR Test: Ultraleise 75%-Tastatur für Büro & Gaming - Smartzone
findings.note: "Deaktiviert ihr beides, lasst die Abtastraten jedoch auf Maximum, sind es bis zu 20 Tage." Implied draw: 8,000 mAh / 160 h = 50 mAh per hour. Smartzone gives 8,000 mAh as Gamakay's figure.
